title: DEWALT Angle Grinder, One-Touch Guard, 4-1/2 -Inch (DWE4011)
description:
About this item
7 amp AC/DC, 12,000 rpm motor of the angle grinder is designed for faster material removal and higher overload protection
One-Touch guard of the metal grinder eliminates the need for a tool to adjust the guard location.
Hex wrench replaces spanner wrench of DEWALT angle grinder - hex wrench can be found in most tool boxes
Quick-Change wheel release allows tool-free wheel removal without the need for a wrench
2-position removable side handle provides increased comfort and control
Slim, ergonomic body design provides increased comfort in extended use applications
5/8-inch 11 spindle thread accepts a wide range of 4-1/2=inch accessories

reviews_1s: Bought this grinder 4 months ago, using in my home shop, not commercial use at all. Tried to use it today, wouldn't spin when the motor turned on, and then white smoke started drifting from inside the casement. I've used this probably 5 hours worth of actual work. I actually have an older one (cuz I'm lazy and don't want to switch from grinder wheel to cutting wheel, so two is luxurious), still works fine. Thought dewalt was a good brand...rethinking.smoke and sparks started comeing out in less then 1 hour of part time useCenter screw got stuck the first time I tried to set the disc, and now it won't fully tighten, and I can't get it to come off. I am fully depressing the button on the back and putting a lot of effort into trying to turn it with the hex wrench or by hand, but it won't budge at all. I'm going to have to buy another tool to try and unlock it, or just give up and get another grinder.Missing the center screw wrench (flat with two prongs). I should have listened to the other reviews that indicated this was the case. Has cheap deflector adjustment lever. Didn't even turn on. Included an allen wrench with no instructions for what it was to be used to torque. Couldn't wait to go through the claim process. Instead, bought a Milwaukee at a big box. I paid about 20$ more and am completely satisfied. Usually Dewalt is good quality for the price. However, this was an epic failure.these grinders are junk, not the same you buy at home depot etc. these start rumbling noise after first hour of use and it gets worse the longer you use it. definitely get protection pln...your gonna need it. bought 6 of these and all are the sameDangerous? YES. Quality? Not too much. The unit arrived promptly but when I opened the box there was no wrench for the wheel lock-nut. What was included was a hex / allen wrench which fit nothing at all on the unit. I was able to use a universal wrench I had in my toolbox. I loaded a disc and started my first cut. It cut fine BUT would not turn off no matter where the switch was placed!! Yes, it does have a "Lock-in-the-ON-Position" switch option but moving it deliberately to "OFF" left the motor running full out. I had to pull the plug in order to stop the grinder. My curiosity got the best of me and I tore it down to find the switch was binding. A machine such as this should never go out to a customer with this condition. Are these defective "Seconds" being sold?Motor literally caught fire after 3 minutes of use. Immediately unplugged and removed from the garage. Hosed down the flaming unit for 2 minutes and it was still sizzling like bacon. Scary.Tool is dangerous, after about 2 hours of use with a 2 1/2" Osborn steel brush, on/off switch would not turn off grinder. I bought two tools at the same time and both switches failed making the tools too dangerous to use. Have not contacted Dewalt yet but will. Will update once resolution confirmed. At least one other feedback from another individual annotated a similar experience. I do not recommend this tool if planning on using continuous. Two tools bought at the same time with similar failures indicates a design flaw where the switch fails due to high temperatures generated from extended run times.Power switch would turn on but not turn off when plugged in. Had to unplug while grinder was running so switch would turn off.I never really got a chance to use it. I plugged it in, out of the box, with the sliding on/off switch in the ‘off’ position, and it turned on. I toggled the switch back and forth to on/off and it stayed on. I had a buddy take a look to see if there was something I was missing. There wasn’t. Plugged in, it was on no matter what. I returned it within 48 hours of receiving it.
